To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the linear SPM kernels based on sparse coding can be used to replace the nonlinear SPM kernel for image classification, and that this new linear kernel is even better than its nonlinear counterpart.

(1) linear SPM based sparse codes of local descriptors is a powerful tool for image categorization, (2) linear SPM kernels are as effective as their nonlinear counterparts in many applications, and (3) linear SVMs using SPM kernels based on sparse codes can scale up to large datasets.
(1) the linear kernel based on sparse coding is more effective than the nonlinear kernel based on histograms in SPM, and (2) the sparse coding of SPM is more effective than SIFT descriptors in SPM.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and analysis of efficient linear SPM kernels for large-scale image classification.
the design of a linear SVM kernel for image categorization.
the development of a linear SPM approach for image categorization, which is both theoretically sound and practically useful.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the proposed linear SPM kernel using sparse coding of Sift descriptors achieves the highest classification accuracy on all the datasets we tested, and the best accuracy on all but the largest of the datasets.
the proposed linear SPM kernel is the most accurate and efficient approach for image categorization to the best of our knowledge.
the linear SPM with sparse coding of SPM descriptors outperforms the state-of-the-art in image categorization, and is the best linear kernel for image classification to date.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, by using the proposed linear SPM kernel, we can obtain the same or even better classification performance as the nonlinear SPM kernel while achieving a significant reduction in training complexity from O(n2 ~n3) to O(n) and a constant in test complexity.
we propose a linear kernel for SPM that is more efficient than nonlinear SPM kernels in both training and testing, and at the same time is even more accurate in image classification.
, for image categorization, linear SPM kernels using sparse SIFT codes are more effective than the nonlinear SIFT kernel or the nonlinear SPM kernel using SIFT histograms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed linear kernel based on SPM using sparse coding of SIFTs achieves the best of both worlds: high classification accuracy of nonlinear SVMs with linear computational complexity.
the SPM method can be extended to other types of image features beyond histograms, and that the resulting linear SPM kernel is a simple yet effective approach for image classification.
linear SPM based sparse coding can achieve state-of-the-art classification performance, while being much faster than the original SPM kernel.
